tools.name: scanruler_status
tools.description: Whether a ScanRuler page is connected to this agent, which version and plugins it has, whether its tab is hidden (page.hidden), and — when none is — how the user connects one. session, with a page, says what it holds: the scan, the project’s name, whether it has changes not saved (unsaved), and its work counted — elements, features, notes … — so a session someone else left is seen before it is replaced (scan_open with saveTo keeps it). page.since: when the page loaded. page.stale, when there: the page could not load a part of the app (an answer said stale_page) — it is older than the app it came from, rebuilt since: save the project, then ask the person to reload, as page.staleNote says. lastProject: the project file last opened or saved through this server — what to open again when the page reloaded (an answer then says pageReloaded). backend says whether ScanRuler runs in a tab (page) or in this server (headless). jobs lists the calls that change the session still running and the latest five others, newest first, each running, done or failed, a running one with progress: { phase, percent } when the page has said how far it is — a call whose answer you did not get is among them; scanruler_wait { for: "job", job } gives its answer, also for a job of an earlier copy of this server, which the page remembers; jobsMore counts the older ones kept. folders: where a scan or a project was opened from or saved into, the latest first — what scanruler_write writes into, scanruler_files lists and scanruler_read reads; kept when the server restarts. server.answerWithin: the seconds a call is held at most before it answers with its job. server.now: the time on this computer, local, with its offset from UTC (2026-10-23T18:04:05+02:00) — the clock to date a report or time a step by. server.cwd: the folder this server started in; server.relativeTo: the folder every relative path is taken from — the latest of folders, else cwd; server.outDir: where a file goes that no path was given for — but an answer too long to carry (truncated: true, file), and a picture in a batch without a path, go into scanruler-work in the folder the scan open now was opened from, when it was opened here by a path — the server’s own files, kept apart from the person’s (scanruler_files { path: "scanruler-work" } lists them, scanruler_read reads them). server.version is this server’s, server.latest the newest on npm when known, server.handedOffFrom the older copy that started this one in its place. server.role: holder — this copy holds the port and the tab’s connection; relay — another copy (another chat or AI app) holds them and this one sends its calls through it, the work still running in the tab, server.holder.version saying which (null: from before 0.4.1); none — neither yet, server.error saying why. serverTooOld, when there, says the server the page is connected to is older than the page needs — while relaying, the holding copy, not this one: tell the person once, in its words, and change nothing yourself unless they ask you to update it. tools, when there, says the tools you were given are not the ones the page offers now (stale): which were added, removed or changed — named the first time, counted after — and which page they were listed from.

tools.name: scanruler_open
tools.description: Open ScanRuler in the user’s default browser, paired with this server, and wait for the page to connect — for when scanruler_status says none is. The first time, ScanRuler warns the user that what you read goes to you and your model, and connects only once they accept; then the browser asks whether the site may reach apps on this computer, and they must allow it. Returns the status, with opened: whether the browser was asked to open it. If connected is still false, tell the user what howToConnect says.

tools.name: scanruler_wait
tools.description: Wait until a ScanRuler page is connected (for: "page", the default), or until it is also done with what it is busy with and every change still running has finished (for: "idle" — then finished lists the changes done or failed since the last such answer, a failed one with its error, and state says idle or running; running, with busy — what the page is at, in its words: a model's build names the step in play and how long it has run — and running, the change still running, with runningS), or until a job is done (for: "job" with job — a call started with wait: false, one answered queued, or one whose answer did not come; scanruler_status lists them). Returns the status — for idle only connected, state and finished, and busy and running while running — or for a job its answer: { job, tool, state, ms, result } or { …, error: { code, message } } — state running if the time ran out first, with runningMs and, once the page has said how far it is, progress: { phase, percent } (its status line: "Measuring deviation", 42): call it again. A picture the job's tool gave comes with that answer, as an image. A job of an earlier copy of this server is read from the page's record of it (session.recent), from says so; that keeps no picture. It waits 45 s at most, this server's answer limit, whatever timeoutSeconds says. connected is false if the time ran out waiting for a page.

job.description: The job to wait for, with for: "job" — as a call with wait: false, a queued answer or scanruler_status gave it.

timeoutSeconds.description: How long to wait at most, seconds — 120 by default, and never past 45.

tools.name: scanruler_write
tools.description: Write a text file — a report, notes, a table of readings — next to the scan, as UTF-8: .md, .txt, .csv, .json only, and only inside the folder this server last opened a scan or a project from (scan_open, project_load) or saved one into (saveTo), or a folder under it. A relative path is taken in that folder; an absolute one must lie in one of those folders, and a path may not climb out with "..". Hidden folders and files, and files agents and tools take instructions or settings from (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, package.json and the like), are refused: pick another name. A file already there is replaced. Returns its path and size in bytes. Refused while this server has opened no scan or project from a folder — then open the scan with scan_open first, or write the file yourself.

path.description: The file: a name in the scan’s folder ("report.md"), a path under it ("report/sigma.md"), or an absolute path in it — .md, .txt, .csv, .json.

text.description: What the file holds, as text.

tools.name: scanruler_files
tools.description: The files in the folder this server last opened a scan or a project from, or saved one into — kept when the server restarts — or in a folder under it (path): each file's name, size in bytes and kind (mesh, project, step, picture, drawing, text or other), newest first, and the folders in it. Where scanruler_write's reports and the files saved beside the scan are; up to 300 entries. Refused while no scan or project has been opened from a folder.

path.description: A folder under the scan’s folder, relative to it or absolute; or one of the folders scanruler_status lists. Leave out for the scan’s folder.

tools.name: scanruler_read
tools.description: A text file read part by part: .md, .txt, .csv, .json, .jsonl, in the folder this server last opened a scan or a project from, or saved one into, in a folder under it, or in one of the folders scanruler_status lists — or an answer too long to carry (truncated: true, file), wherever it was written. A relative path is taken in the first of those folders, and a path may not climb out with "..". Returns { text, offset, nextOffset, size }, in bytes of the file: nextOffset, when there, is where to read on from; without it the text reaches the file's end. An answer holds at most 40 k characters. Refused for any other kind of file, and, but for such an answer, while no scan or project has been opened from a folder.

path.description: The file: a name in the scan’s folder, a path under it ("scanruler-work/report.json"), or an absolute path.

offset.description: Where to start, in bytes: the last answer’s nextOffset. The file’s start by default.

limit.description: The most bytes to read, a whole character at least; as many as an answer holds by default, and never more.

tools.name: scanruler_batch
tools.description: Run several of the ScanRuler tools in one call, in order, each with its own arguments — a run of scan_nearest, element_fit or section_get calls, say. Returns results, one per call in order: { tool, ok, result } or { tool, ok: false, error: { code, message } }. The first refused stops the rest (stopped says which index, failed: { index, tool, error } which call) unless stopOnError is false. notes, when a call answered with the notes left for you, is the last call’s, repeated at the top. When the refused call is a change, then with rollback (the default) every change the batch made before it is undone, so the batch stands or falls whole: undone names the steps taken back, newest first, callsUndone counts the calls, and each of those answers ok: false and undone: true, its result kept as it was. Before anything runs, the names the calls would give new things (a command that says which of its fields name them, in one name space) are checked against each other: two alike — case and spaces at the ends aside — refuse the batch with nothing run, naming both calls; a name the session already has is the page’s to refuse. A refused read — section_get, scan_query, any tool that changes nothing — undoes nothing: what came before it stands (kept says so). A call refused busy is run again once the page is idle (retried: "busy" on its result). Each call that changes the session is still its own undo step. build: "end" builds a modelled part once for a run of changes to it — sketches edited one after another, say — rather than after each: every call but the last is sent deferred, and a change so sent answers before its rebuild (build: "held", its result and bodies the part as last built; a pick by index names a face of that part); the last call builds them all, and so does a read of the part, or any other kind of tool, met on the way. timings: true gives each call its ms and the batch total_ms, and a change's build the steps it played with their ms (result.steps.played). wait: false answers at once with { queued, job }, and so does a batch still running at the server’s answer limit (with after, its seconds); scanruler_wait { for: "job", job } gives the batch's answer. A { "$file": path } anywhere in a call’s arguments is that JSON file’s contents, and { "$file": path, "$at": "loops.0.points" } the part of it there (keys and indices by dots). A call’s to writes its answer to a .json file in place of carrying it — a long reading fed on to a later call by $file, not through the conversation. A relative path is taken from the folder of the scan or project last opened or saved (scanruler_status: server.relativeTo) — before any, from /pkg. A tool that returns a picture is not shown here: the picture is written to a file — its call’s path, or a new file in scanruler-work in the folder the scan open now was opened from (by scan_open or project_load with a path), else in /pkg — and its result gives that file.path (and file.folder, the scanruler-work folder); call the tool directly to see the picture. The server’s own tools (scanruler_status, _open, _wait, _batch, _write, _files, _read, _tools) cannot be batched.

calls.description: The calls, in order — or give file instead.

tool.description: A tool’s name, as listed — scan_nearest, element_fit.

arguments.description: Its arguments, as the tool takes them; {} for none.

to.description: A .json file its answer is written to, whole, in place of carrying it here — a long reading (outlines, a grid, a description) a later call takes as { "$file": to, "$at": "loops.0.points" }. The result then says where (written: { path, bytes }) and what the answer holds (keys, a list’s length). A file there already is replaced.

file.description: A JSON file of the calls, read here in place of calls: [{ tool, arguments }], or [{ name, input }] by the command's own name (scan.open), or either under "calls" or "steps". For a long run a script wrote, which then need not pass through the conversation. A relative path is taken from the folder of the scan or project last opened or saved (scanruler_status: server.relativeTo) — before any, from /pkg.

stopOnError.description: Stop at the first refused call (the default), or run every call and report each.

rollback.description: When the batch stops at a refused change, undo what it changed before it (the default) — or leave those changes standing (false). A refused read undoes nothing either way.

build.description: each (the default): a change rebuilds the part before it answers. end: the changes build once, at the last call.

timings.description: Each call’s ms, the batch’s total_ms, and the steps a change’s build played with their ms.

wait.description: false: answer { queued: true, job } at once and run on; scanruler_wait { for: "job", job } gives the answer. true, the default: answer when done — or queued all the same past the server’s answer limit.

tools.name: align_auto
tools.description: Read a coordinate system off the scan and apply it, as Auto-align then Confirm alignment do: the directions most faces are square to and the axis round walls run along, the part standing on its base, its long side along X. level: settled (the default) lays all the faces on the axes at once, by area; largest squares the largest flat face exactly and settles the rest about its normal. Returns what the pose was read from, the transform, how many elements moved, and square — how square it came out: largest (the largest flat face’s axis, area, tiltDeg) and per axis the faces square to it with their tilts; largestInside when that face looks into the part (the scan stands in front of it: a rib’s wall, not a mating face — level on the mating face with align.datum). Trap: a drafted wall reads as its draft, not as an alignment error. One undo step.

level.description: settled (the default): all faces at once, by area. largest: the largest flat face exactly, the rest settled about its normal.

detail.description: brief (the default): the transform and how many elements moved. full: every element where it now is.

wait.description: false: answer { queued: true, job } at once and run on; scanruler_wait { for: "job", job } gives the answer. true, the default: answer when done — or queued all the same past the server’s answer limit.

timings.description: true: the answer adds ms and, where the change built, steps.played — each step with its ms.

tools.description: Put the part back in the coordinates the scanner delivered it in, with everything measured on it. Returns how many elements moved with it. One undo step.

wait.description: false: answer { queued: true, job } at once and run on; scanruler_wait { for: "job", job } gives the answer. true, the default: answer when done — or queued all the same past the server’s answer limit.

timings.description: true: the answer adds ms and, where the change built, steps.played — each step with its ms.

tools.name: align_datum
tools.description: A 3-2-1 alignment, as the panel’s alignment box sets it up: primary levels the part — a plane (or 3 points, or plane { origin, normal }: a level’s plane from scan.heightmap { levels: true }) whose outward normal becomes primaryAxis (default z-); secondary turns it — a line or axis (or 2 points) laid along secondaryAxis (default x+), or a plane; origin is the zero point — a point, sphere or circle (or 1 point). Elements by id or name, or points in mm used as given, not snapped. Trap: a plane as secondary puts its outward NORMAL on secondaryAxis, not its face along it. Each datum zeroes the coordinates it owns, the origin only those left open; an origin alone moves without turning. On a first alignment the coordinates nothing sets are centred on the scan’s box (keepFree: true leaves them). Returns the transform applied, how many elements moved, centred, origin { set, at, note } and parallelFace when a face parallel to the levelling plane, 0.3 to 5 mm off it (further on a noisy scan), holds more of the scan. Trap: on an embossed or warped sheet a plane fitted to the outermost faces lies on the bead crowns or the high spots, not the sheet — level on the largest level’s plane instead. One undo step.

points.description: 3 points, mm — they span the face.

origin.description: A point on the plane, mm; it lands on 0 along primaryAxis.

normal.description: Its outward normal: out of the face, away from the material.

plane.description: A plane as given — a level’s plane from scan.heightmap { levels: true }.

primary.description: Levelling: an element, 3 points on the scan, or a plane { origin, normal }.

primaryAxis.description: The axis the primary’s outward normal becomes; default z-.

points.description: 2 points, mm — they run along the edge.

secondary.description: Rotation: an element, or 2 points on the scan.

secondaryAxis.description: The axis the secondary runs along (a plane: its normal); default x+.

element.description: An element for the zero point.

point.description: A point for the zero point, mm.

origin.description: The zero point: an element, or a point on the scan.

keepFree.description: First alignment: leave the coordinates nothing sets where they are instead of centring.

detail.description: brief (the default): the transform and how many elements moved. full: every element where it now is.

wait.description: false: answer { queued: true, job } at once and run on; scanruler_wait { for: "job", job } gives the answer. true, the default: answer when done — or queued all the same past the server’s answer limit.

timings.description: true: the answer adds ms and, where the change built, steps.played — each step with its ms.

tools.name: align_symmetry
tools.description: Settle the part’s pose on its mirror plane and apply it, as Use symmetry then Confirm alignment do: the pose is Auto-align’s, the mirror plane a measured symmetry plane or one searched for on the scan; the axis nearest its normal is turned onto it and the zero point put on it. Refuses when the scan has no symmetry plane. Returns the note on what it settled on, the transform and how many elements moved. One undo step.

detail.description: brief (the default): the transform and how many elements moved. full: every element where it now is.

wait.description: false: answer { queued: true, job } at once and run on; scanruler_wait { for: "job", job } gives the answer. true, the default: answer when done — or queued all the same past the server’s answer limit.

timings.description: true: the answer adds ms and, where the change built, steps.played — each step with its ms.

annotations.title: Align the part on its symmetry plane

tools.name: deviation_align
tools.description: Rigid best fit (no scale) of the scan onto the reference part, then the deviation map under it. mode auto (the default) finds the pose on its own; points starts from three or more pairs of corresponding points (scan and reference, mm) then refines; local refines the fit in hand on a marked surface only (vertices), within searchDistance mm. Returns the alignment (RMS, points matched, transform) and the map’s statistics. One undo step.

reference.description: The same point on the reference, mm.

vertices.description: local: the surface to refine on, scan vertex numbers.

searchDistance.description: local: how far a point may lie from the reference to count, mm.

wait.description: false: answer { queued: true, job } at once and run on; scanruler_wait { for: "job", job } gives the answer. true, the default: answer when done — or queued all the same past the server’s answer limit.

timings.description: true: the answer adds ms and, where the change built, steps.played — each step with its ms.

annotations.title: Best-fit the scan onto the reference

tools.name: deviation_export
tools.description: The deviation map as a file of readings, for working on it elsewhere: side "scan" (the default) a reading per scan vertex with its signed distance from the reference (or the element measured against), side "reference" a reading per sample on the reference; format ply (the default, binary), npy (N × 4 float32 x, y, z, d) or csv. Returns the file with readings, measured, withinTolerance, withinTolerancePct, tolerance and searchDistance. Trap: the distance is NaN where there is no reading, and a reading past the search distance is kept as it is — |d| ≤ searchDistance says it counts. Changes nothing. The file is written to `path`; the result says where and how large it is, not its bytes.

side.description: The readings: per scan vertex (the default), or per sample on the reference.

path.description: Where to write the file: a file path — one there already is replaced — or a folder (one there, or a path ending in /) to write it into under the name ScanRuler gives it, numbered past a file of that name there (-2, -3 …). Without it, it goes into /pkg the same way. A relative path is taken from the folder of the scan or project last opened or saved (scanruler_status: server.relativeTo) — before any, from /pkg.

tools.name: deviation_hotspots
tools.description: The deviation map read as patches: the vertices past the tolerance gathered into connected regions, the largest and farthest first — where the part is off, how large each place is and by how much. Needs a map (deviation.align or deviation.set_target). Returns each patch’s centroid, box, area, count, mean, extreme, depth, volume, kind ("feature": material missing or misplaced, to model or name; "texture": roughness), side, the extreme’s point and vertex, a few vertices, and onReference; features, found, over and unmeasured; on: "reference" reads the map on the reference, adding noScan. Trap: read far every time — the vertices past the search distance, which the map draws bare: far.inside is scan deep inside the reference (a hole, pocket or slot the model lacks), far.outside scan standing off it. Changes nothing.

tolerance.description: ± mm; the map’s tolerance by default.

patches.description: How many patches to name; 8 by default, 50 at most.

grain.description: mm two vertices over tolerance may lie apart and be one patch; three point spacings by default.

on.description: The map read: on the scan (the default) or on the reference.

annotations.title: Where the deviation lies over tolerance

tools.name: deviation_measure
tools.description: Measure the deviation map again under the alignment in hand — after a change of facing limit or search distance, say. deviation.align measures it already. Returns the map’s statistics (min, max, mean, RMS, sigma, share within the tolerance, points matched). One undo step.

wait.description: false: answer { queued: true, job } at once and run on; scanruler_wait { for: "job", job } gives the answer. true, the default: answer when done — or queued all the same past the server’s answer limit.

timings.description: true: the answer adds ms and, where the change built, steps.played — each step with its ms.

tools.name: deviation_open_reference
tools.description: Open the nominal part the scan is compared with — STEP from CAD, or STL, PLY, OBJ or 3MF — in place of the one there is; any alignment and map against the old one go, the elements measured on the scan stay. Returns the deviation state. Not undoable: a new reference starts a new history. The file is read from `path` on this computer and streamed to the page.

name.description: The file's name with its extension — "bracket.step". Defaults to the file's own name.

units.description: The file’s units: mm (the default), cm, m or in. Everything is measured in mm once read.

path.description: The file to read, on this computer: an absolute path, or a relative one. A relative path is taken from the folder of the scan or project last opened or saved (scanruler_status: server.relativeTo) — before any, from /pkg.

wait.description: false: answer { queued: true, job } at once and run on; scanruler_wait { for: "job", job } gives the answer. true, the default: answer when done — or queued all the same past the server’s answer limit.

timings.description: true: the answer adds ms and, where the change built, steps.played — each step with its ms.

tools.name: deviation_set_target
tools.description: Map how far the scan strays from one of its own fitted elements — a plane, cylinder, cone, sphere or torus — instead of from a reference part; null goes back to the reference. side is the material side, read off the scan when the element is chosen (outward: the element’s outer side; inward: a bore or shell) — give it to override. facingDeg limits which surface counts to what faces the element within that many degrees, null for any. Needs the viewport. Returns the map’s statistics. One undo step.

side.description: The material side; read off the scan by default.

facingDeg.description: The facing limit, degrees, or null for any.

wait.description: false: answer { queued: true, job } at once and run on; scanruler_wait { for: "job", job } gives the answer. true, the default: answer when done — or queued all the same past the server’s answer limit.

tools.name: deviation_settings
tools.description: The deviation map’s reading: range (colour scale, ± mm), maxDistance (search distance, mm), bands, tolerance (± mm the statistics count within), facingDeg (a change measures the map again), colormap (the person’s own choice, kept outside the undo — read settings.colormap for the ramp before judging a picture), on (which surface a map against the reference is painted on; read both sides) and show (the map switch; false leaves the surface bare, the map still measured). Returns the deviation state. Trap: the map paints in the Deviation workspace only — workspace.set deviation brings it back, and view.render says which map it painted (map) or why none (mapWhy). One undo step.

bands.description: Stepped colours, or null for smooth.

colormap.description: jet (blue inside, green on the surface, red outside) or a perceptual ramp.

on.description: The surface the map is painted on; scan by default.

show.description: The map painted (true) or the surface left bare (false).

tools.name: deviation_volume
tools.description: The scan and the reference part compared as solids, on a grid of small cells: each cell inside one and not the other is an error, touching cells a region. Read it before the surface patches — it tells how much material is wrong and where, which the nearest-point map cannot: excess is material the reference has and the part has not, missing the other way round, unsure where the scan does not say (never an error). Needs deviation.align. Returns totals (mm³ and % of the reference) and the regions largest first, each with kind, volume, maxDepth, thickness, shape (layer or lump), centroid, deepest, box, evidence and confidence. Trap: nothing thinner than smallestSeen (two cells) is seen — the surface map stays the tool for fine offsets. About 15 s on a 1.5M-triangle scan. Changes nothing kept.

tolerance.description: ± mm; the map’s tolerance by default.

cell.description: The cell, mm; by default half the tolerance or a 250th of the reference’s longest side, the larger.

regions.description: How many regions to name; 8 by default, 50 at most.

within.description: Only this box is looked at, in the reference’s frame.

kinds.description: Only regions of these kinds named; all by default. The totals are of all.

tools.name: dimension_add
tools.description: Measure between elements, or a size or tolerance of one, as the panel’s dimension box does. refs are the elements by id or name, in slot order (a section counts as the plane it was cut on). Without type, the type follows the elements as clicking them does — two planes their distance, a plane and an axis theirs, and so on; with type, one of dist-point-point, dist-point-axis, dist-point-plane, dist-axis-axis, dist-axis-plane, dist-plane-plane, angle-axis-axis, angle-axis-plane, angle-plane-plane, size-diameter, form-flatness, form-cylindricity, form-circularity, form-sphericity, orient-parallelism, orient-perpendicularity, orient-angularity, loc-coaxiality (the measure-reference guide lists each one’s slots). anchor, for two spheres: center (default), gap or span; limit holds the value to a ceiling or a nominal ± band. Returns the dimension with its value (mm or degrees, finer than the panel shows), the formatted value and the verdict. One undo step.

anchor.description: Two spheres: centre to centre (the default), the gap between them, or the span across them.

max.description: The most the value may be, mm or degrees.

kind.description: A nominal with an allowance either side.

nominal.description: The nominal value, mm or degrees.

limit.description: What the value is checked against, for a pass or fail verdict.

tools.name: guide_read
tools.description: How to do a task with ScanRuler: the workflow, the judgement and the traps the tools’ own descriptions do not carry, written for this build — read the guide for your task, whole, before its first step, and a section again when you need it. The guides: measure — measuring a 3D scan: fitting elements, dimensions and GD&T-like checks, sections and the 2D sheet, deviation against a reference part, wall thickness, the report — by hand or as an automatic run over many scans; measure-reference — the measuring tools’ shapes with examples, what each answer costs, what each refusal means — a section at a time, as the measure guide sends you. topic: a guide, or several read in order (a guide and the ones it is read with, in one call) — as many as fit in about 60 k characters, the rest named in next, to read in the next call. A guide longer than that by itself answers its sections in order while they fit, and names the rest in sectionsLeft, each to read by section. A guide’s sections for one moment of the task — measuring, building — are not in the whole read: later names each with when to read it, and the note says how; read it by section when that moment comes, before the step it is for. section: one section of one guide, by its heading — the index lists them, with when to read those a whole read leaves for later. A long section with ### parts under it — a reference’s list of command shapes — is best read by those parts: section takes a ### heading too, the one part you need. With no topic, the index: each guide with its sections and what each costs in tokens. Changes nothing.

tools.name: project_save
tools.description: The session as a .scanruler project file, as Save Project downloads it: the scan, the reference, the image and every measurement, each rebuilt when it is opened. Needs the browser. Returns the file’s bytes and its name, holds (what is in it, counted — read it before calling the file a revision: a page reset holds no model), aligned (whether the scan stands in an aligned frame) and says (what a workspace wants said of the work saved). The file is written to `path`; the result says where and how large it is, not its bytes.

tools.name: report_get
tools.description: The measurement report. format "text" is word for word what the workspace’s Copy report button gives — measure (elements and dimensions with verdicts), deviation, thickness or flat (2D). format "json" (the default) is the whole session’s report structured: what the numbers rest on (units, scale, frame, alignment, fit method, outlier cut-offs), every element with its fit, every dimension with value, unit, limit and verdict, the tally of checks, the sections, and the deviation, thickness and 2D results with their settings.

workspace.description: For text: whose report — measure (the default), deviation, thickness or flat.

tools.name: scan_draft
tools.description: The scan’s walls that run near a pull direction — the sides a mould opens along — gathered into patches, each with draftDeg, the angle it leans off the pull: positive where the wall faces partly along the pull, negative where it faces back (a back draft, an undercut); with sigmaDeg, spreadDeg, centroid, box, area (mm²), count, facing, turnDeg and round for a boss’s or hole’s round side. Needs pull; box, nearDeg (10), patches (12), minArea (1 mm²) and split (a plane no patch reaches across: "symmetry", a plane element, "XY", "YZ", "XZ" or { point, normal }) narrow it. Trap: read it early on a moulded or cast part, along each direction the tools open — walls that lean half a degree to a few explain fits that miss by the lean. Changes nothing.

box.description: Only the scan inside this box.

split.description: Keep every patch to one side of this plane.

annotations.title: Read the draft against a pull

tools.name: scan_fit_surface
tools.description: A patch of the scan measured as a surface — a sloped side, a twisted ruled face, a dome, a saddle — from vertices or a box (normal keeps those facing a way). Returns the patch’s frame (origin, normal, basisU, basisV) and each model as a height over (u, v): plane (a + b·u + c·v), bilinear (+ d·u·v) and quadric (+ d·u² + e·u·v + f·v², with curvature { k1, k2, r1, r2, axis1, axis2, shape }), each with coefficients, rms and worst; model: best (the default) fits every one and names the simplest whose rms is within a tenth of the lowest. Trap: 7 points at least, at most limit (20000) spread evenly. Changes nothing.

vertices.description: The scan vertices of the patch.

box.description: The scan inside a box, in place of vertices.

normal.description: With box: only the vertices facing this way.

model.description: Which surface; best (the default) fits each and names the simplest that holds.

limit.description: How many points at most; 20000 by default.

annotations.title: Fit a sloped or curved patch

tools.name: scan_heightmap
tools.description: Where the scan is first met looking along an axis (axis, -z by default: the top surface from above) or square onto a plane (plane: an element, "XY", "YZ", "XZ", or { origin, normal, u? }), over a grid of cells: pocket floors, ledges, a step's height, a face's tilt, a pad's tiers, an icon on a key in one call. of: height (the default), deviation (the map's reading where each ray lands) or relief (the height less the surface round it, for icons, grooves and lettering). Returns cell, origin [u0, v0], cols, rows, grid (rows of mm from the low v up, null where nothing; grid[r][c] stands at u0 + (c + ½)·cell, v0 + (r + ½)·cell), min, max, hit, valued; with plane also its frame (a cell's point is origin + u·U + v·V + height·normal). levels: true gives the values gathered into levels in place of the grid, largest first — of a height, each holding 5 % of the map or more with its plane { origin, normal } (fitted to its cells, normal towards the viewer), which align.datum { primary: { plane } } levels on: the sheet itself, not its bead crowns; a gentle warp that ran levels together is taken out first and said (warp { rise, bow, note }); picture: true adds the map coloured. Trap: with plane, box is [u, v, height] in the plane's frame (or { world }), and scanLies says where the scan lies when few cells meet it. Changes nothing. The picture comes back as an image; with `path` it is written to a file too, and with `inline: false` only there.

min.description: Lowest corner, mm ([u, v, height] with plane).

max.description: Highest corner, mm ([u, v, height] with plane).

world.description: A box in the world, in place of min and max.

box.description: The part looked at; the scan’s box by default. With plane: [u, v, height], or world: { min, max }.

axis.description: The way looked: -z (the default) from above, +z from below, ±x, ±y.

origin.description: A point on the plane, mm.

normal.description: Its normal: the side looked from.

u.description: A direction for u, flattened into the plane; a sketch’s by default.

plane.description: Look square onto this plane instead of along an axis.

flip.description: With plane: look from its other side.

of.description: height (the default), deviation (the map’s, where the ray lands) or relief (height less the surface round it).

smooth.description: relief: the smoothing sigma, mm; three cells by default.

grid.description: The grid of numbers (the default unless levels); false returns the picture alone.

levels.description: Gather the values into levels, largest first, in place of the grid; of a height, a warp taken out first when it ran two together, and each level of 5 % or more with its plane.

gap.description: levels: the least gap between two levels, mm.

slopeDeg.description: levels of a height: cells steeper are left out, degrees; 10 by default, 90 keeps every one.

picture.description: Add a picture of the map with a scale.

path.description: Also write the picture to a file: a file path — one there already is replaced — or a folder (one there, or a path ending in /) to write it into under the name ScanRuler gives it, numbered past a picture of that name there (-2, -3 …). Without it, it is only shown — but in scanruler_batch, which shows no picture, it is written under a new name into the folder of the scan or project last opened or saved (the latest of scanruler_status folders), before any into /pkg. A relative path is taken from the folder of the scan or project last opened or saved (scanruler_status: server.relativeTo) — before any, from /pkg.

inline.description: false, with path: the picture is written to the file and not shown — the answer says where. A picture costs far more context than its text; save the ones you only deliver.

tools.name: scan_nearest
tools.description: Where a place lands on the scan: the vertex (a point snaps to the nearest), its coordinates and outward normal, a triangle it is a corner of, and how far it lies from the point asked about. Use it to check a point lies on the surface before fitting there.

point.description: [x, y, z] mm in the current frame; the nearest scan vertex is taken.

screen.description: A viewport pixel [x, y] (not available yet).

candidate.description: A feature from scan.candidates (not available yet).

tools.name: scan_open
tools.description: Open a mesh as the scan to measure — STL, PLY, OBJ or 3MF, or a STEP part cut into triangles — in place of the one there is; everything measured on the old one goes with it, so it refuses while the session holds measurements unless discard is true (the refusal names what is held). A reference part opened from a file stays, its alignment and maps gone (referenceKept); one made from the session’s own work goes (referenceDropped). Returns the scan: name, units, vertex and triangle counts, bounding box, centre and diagonal (size), mm. Not undoable: a new scan starts a new history. The file is read from `path` on this computer and streamed to the page. With `saveTo`, the session is saved as a project file there first (as project_save does), then replaced as with discard: true — one call to keep what a page holds and start anew.

name.description: The file's name with its extension — "ballbar.stl". Defaults to the file's own name.

units.description: The file’s units: mm (the default), cm, m or in. Everything is measured in mm once read.

discard.description: true: replace the session though it holds measurements (lost unless saved as a project first). Refused otherwise when there is work to lose.

A relative path is taken from the folder of the scan or project last opened or saved (scanruler_status: server.relativeTo) — before any, from /pkg. A folder opens the one mesh file in it (.stl, .ply, .obj, .3mf); with more than one, the answer lists them.

If the save fails nothing is replaced. The answer says where it went (savedTo). A relative path is taken from the folder of the scan or project last opened or saved (scanruler_status: server.relativeTo) — before any, from /pkg.

tools.name: scan_outline
tools.description: The scan’s outline seen along an axis, or square onto a plane, read as a sketch would draw it: a flange’s plan, a bezel’s opening, a gasket’s shape — each loop as the fewest lines and arcs that follow it within tolerance (mm, 0.2 by default), a round loop as one circle. axis, plane, flip and box as scan.heightmap takes them, u, v as it lays them. Returns loops, the largest first (4 by default): hole, area (mm²), box, points ([u, v] corners), rounds { at, radius, center }, arcs { from, radius, center, mid } (from points[from] through mid to the next point: mid says which way it bulges, a slot’s half-round end too) or circle { center, radius, rms }, and worst (mm the trace strays from what is drawn, worstAt when past the tolerance). Changes nothing.

axis.description: The way looked: -z (the default) from above, and so on.

origin.description: A point on the plane, mm.

normal.description: Its normal: the side looked from.

u.description: A direction for u, flattened into the plane.

plane.description: Look square onto this plane instead of along an axis.

flip.description: With plane: look from its other side.

min.description: Lowest corner, mm ([u, v, height] with plane).

max.description: Highest corner, mm ([u, v, height] with plane).

tolerance.description: How closely the sketch follows the outline, mm; 0.2 by default.

loops.description: How many loops, the largest first; 4 by default.

tools.name: scan_pattern
tools.description: Rotational repeats about an axis — a fan's blades, a flange's holes, a wheel's spokes, a gear's teeth — counted from the scan: it is cut square to the axis at each height in at, and each cut (between radius.min and radius.max) is turned against itself. Needs axis: a cylinder, cone, line or circle element, "X", "Y", "Z", or { origin, dir }. Returns per height count, pitchDeg, phaseDeg, betweenDeg (angles as section.cut { across: { axis, angleDeg } } takes them), score (0 to 1; under 0.5 count is 1 and tried says the best), rms, worst, instances (each angleDeg, radius, offDeg, rms, worst, share) and rings (round outlines about the axis: radius, off, towardDeg, rms). Trap: features at different heights and radii need a cut through each, radius kept to one ring. Changes nothing.

oneOf.description: A cylinder, cone, line or circle element, or a coordinate axis "X", "Y", "Z".

origin.description: A point on the axis, mm.

axis.description: The axis the copies repeat round.

oneOf.description: A world point, mm: the height of its foot on the axis.

at.description: Heights to cut at; 6 spread over the scan by default.

radius.description: Only the cut between these distances from the axis.

maxCount.description: The most copies looked for; 60 by default.

instances.description: List each copy; true by default.

annotations.title: Count the repeats round an axis

tools.name: scan_qa
tools.description: One call before modelling, to know what the scan will and will not give. Returns rims (the open edges of its holes: count, total length, the longest few with rim number, centre, size and circle where one fits — element.fit { kind: "circle", rim } makes it an element), noise (the median scatter of small plane fits, mm; 0 on a CAD tessellation), tessellation where the mesh is an STL exported from CAD (cad, its facets exactly flat; sparse where its vertices lie only on edges and rims, too far apart to fit on — densifyTo, the edge length to subdivide it to first, noise.measured the bends between facets that a fit would read), thickness through the part along axis (p5, p50, p95, the main faces’ tiltDeg and faces { topDeg, bottomDeg }), sheet where most of the area has a second skin facing back within reach mm (gauge { p5, p50, p95 }, twoSkins: that share), apart on such a part with flat walls (regions standing over reach mm off every main wall — tabs bent in, ribs, bosses: center, box, area mm², largest first) and notes, what looks wrong, plainly. Traps: a scanned skin with no rims, or only pinholes, is a wrap bridging the holes it did not see through; on a sheet, thickness reads the box across the part — the gauge is sheet.gauge. Changes nothing.

tools.name: scan_query
tools.description: The scan’s vertices inside a box, or within a radius of a point (near), with their outward normals — the points on a face, to measure a dimension or a draft off; normal keeps only those facing a direction. Returns matched, the vertex numbers, points and normals (mm, current frame), the box round them, centroid and mean normal; fields: count, ids or all (the default) says how much. Trap: at most limit come back (1000 by default, 20000 at most), every k-th spread evenly, step saying k — mark: true marks every matching vertex, not the thinned list, for element.fit_marked { marked: true }. Changes nothing on the part.

box.description: A box in the current frame.

near.description: A ball about a point, in place of box.

normal.description: Only the vertices whose outward normal faces this way.

limit.description: How many vertices at most; 1000 by default, 20000 at most.

mark.description: Leave every matching vertex marked, for element.fit_marked { marked: true }.

fields.description: count: the numbers alone (the default with mark); ids: with the vertices; all: with points and normals (the default).

tools.name: scan_scale
tools.description: Scale the scan to its true size — a photogrammetry scan (Meshroom, say) has no size of its own, and session.state says noTrueSize when one looks like it. Give references: lengths measured on the scan with their true lengths from the real part — a length dimension already made (distance or diameter), an element’s diameter (sphere, cylinder, circle), or two points — or a factor outright. Several references are averaged by length; each one’s own factor and how far it is off the average (offPct) come back, so a bad one shows. Best references: long, and between centres (hole to hole, ball to ball) — a centre does not move when the surface sits proud or sunk. The scale is about the frame’s zero point: every coordinate times the factor. Elements, dimensions, sections and the alignment scale with it; the fit to a reference part goes. Refuses while a model, notes or other work is built on the scan at the old size (scale first). dryRun: true returns the factor and the size it would give without scaling. Returns factor, the references, size before and after, and the scan. One undo step.

factor.description: Scale by this factor outright, instead of from references — 25.4 for a file in inches read as mm.

dimension.description: A length dimension already measured — a distance or a diameter.

true.description: Its length on the real part, mm.

element.description: A sphere, cylinder or circle; its diameter is the length.

true.description: Its diameter on the real part, mm.

items.description: A point on the scan, mm.

points.description: The two ends of the length.

true.description: The distance between them on the real part, mm.

items.description: A length known two ways: measured on the scan, and true — from calipers on the real part.

references.description: Lengths to scale from — one or more.

dryRun.description: Work out the factor and the size it gives, and scale nothing.

tools.name: scan_segment
tools.description: The scan’s planar regions, found all at once: grown from the flattest places outward within maxDeg (15°) and maxRms (0.05 mm), those smaller than minArea given back. Returns found, considered, claimed, noise and the regions, largest first, at most limit (20): id, normal, point, sigma, area (mm²), box, vertices, neighbours { id, deg, smooth } and, with symmetric, mirror (its twin across that plane). Trap: a round surface comes out as strips that look like facets — such a region says curved { sagitta } and run, and curvedRuns joins them into surfaces with a note saying what to model each as; read the runs before taking regions for faces. mark: a region’s id, or several, leaves their points marked for element.fit_marked { marked: true }. Changes nothing.

kind.description: What to find; plane, the default and for now the only one.

box.description: Only the scan inside this box.

minArea.description: mm²; by default a square 2 % of the scan’s diagonal on a side.

limit.description: How many regions are listed; 20 by default.

symmetric.description: Pair regions mirrored across this plane: a plane element, or "XY", "YZ", "XZ".

oneOf.description: Several regions’ ids, their points together.

mark.description: Leave this region’s points marked, or several regions’.

list.description: With mark: the list of regions too.

tools.name: section_cut
tools.description: Cut the scan with a plane and keep the cut as a section, put on the 2D sheet. across: an element with a direction (plane, cylinder, cone, line, circle) by id or name; "XY", "YZ" or "XZ" through the part’s centre; or { axis, angleDeg }, a plane through an axis turned angleDeg about it — a half section of a turned part. offset slides the plane along its normal, mm (a coordinate plane: the coordinate itself). kind "shadow" keeps the scan’s shadow instead: the whole part projected onto the plane, its outer boundary as loops read as lines and arcs (tolerance, play, smoothDeg), stood up as a block for export.step (extrude). Trap: a shadow takes no offset. Returns the section: its plane and chain count — a shadow also its loops, area and band. One undo step.

axis.description: A cylinder, cone, line or circle, or a coordinate axis "X", "Y", "Z".

across.description: An element with a direction, a coordinate plane, or { axis, angleDeg }.

offset.description: Along the normal, mm. A cut’s only.

kind.description: cut (the default), or shadow: the whole scan projected onto the plane.

play.description: Shadow: clearance outside the part, mm; 1 by default, negative a press fit.

tolerance.description: Shadow: lines and arcs read to this, mm; 0.1 by default.

smoothDeg.description: Shadow: corners turning less than this are rounded, degrees; 30 by default, 0 keeps all sharp.

extrude.description: Shadow: stood up as a block through the part, for export.step; true by default.

wait.description: false: answer { queued: true, job } at once and run on; scanruler_wait { for: "job", job } gives the answer. true, the default: answer when done — or queued all the same past the server’s answer limit.

timings.description: true: the answer adds ms and, where the change built, steps.played — each step with its ms.

tools.name: section_get
tools.description: A section’s cut as polylines: each chain’s points in order — [u, v] mm on the sheet, what flat.fit and a sketch on the section take, or with space "world" or "both" [x, y, z] in the current frame — with the plane (origin, normal, basisU, basisV) and per chain closed, length, points, bounds. Trap: at most limit points over all chains (4000 by default, 50000 at most); past it every k-th point is kept and step says k. chains picks chains by index; skin "outer" or "inner" reads one skin of a thin wall alone, facing the points whose way out lies within withinDeg of dir, each chain then coming back as runs. Changes nothing.

section.description: The section, by id or name.

chains.description: Which chains; every one by default.

space.description: sheet (the default): [u, v]; world: [x, y, z]; both.

limit.description: Points at most over every chain; 4000 by default, 50000 at most.

skin.description: One skin of a thin wall alone.

facing.description: Only the points whose way out of the material lies within withinDeg of dir.

tools.name: section_render
tools.description: A picture of a section as a PNG, for checking a slice against what was built on it: the scan’s cut as points on the sheet ([u, v] mm, +u right, +v up), a mm grid with values in the margins, a scale bar, and the workspaces’ layers over it (a model’s cut as outlines, a sketch’s pieces). Scan points within ten tolerances of an outline are read against it: on it (grey) or off it (red). Needs section, or plane to cut the scan for the picture alone ({ origin, normal }, "XY"/"YZ"/"XZ", an element, or { sketch }). Returns gap { points, read, over, outside, inside, max, rms, overBox }, layers, axes, sheet (origin, normal, basisU, basisV) and map (pixel (c, r) is [left + c·unitsPerPx, top − r·unitsPerPx]). Trap: a plane’s sheet has its zero at the world origin’s foot, a section’s at the part’s centre — read sheet. 800 px by default, up to 2048. Needs the browser. Changes nothing. The picture comes back as an image; with `path` it is written to a file too, and with `inline: false` only there.

layers.description: The layers to draw, by key; every one by default, [] for the scan alone.

Without it, it is only shown — but in scanruler_batch, which shows no picture, it is written under a new name into the folder of the scan or project last opened or saved (the latest of scanruler_status folders), before any into /pkg. tools.name: session_recent
tools.description: What became of the commands an agent’s server ran under its jobs — each change and each batch is one, and the server names it — newest first: the job, the command, running, done or failed, when it started and its ms, and its result or its error { code, message }. A result past 16,000 characters is left out (resultOmitted says its size). The page keeps the last 100 for as long as it stays open, so a server started after the one that asked can still say what a job did. job: only that job’s.

job.description: Only this job’s commands, as the server named it.

tools.description: Close the scan, the reference part and the 2D image, and with them every measurement and the project’s name, as opening an empty project does. With `saveTo`, the session is saved as a project file there first (as project_save does), then replaced as with discard: true — one call to keep what a page holds and start anew.

tools.name: session_state

tools.name: view_render
tools.description: A picture of the 3D view as a PNG — what the viewport shows, without the HTML labels (dimension values, names). view and/or fit turn the view first, as view.set does; frame frames a box or a place (mmAcross says what the picture spans). Trap: only fit: true fits — a view alone keeps the zoom, and a frame stays for the pictures after it (fitted and framedEarlier say so). show puts keys on screen or away for the picture alone ({ scan: false } pictures what was built on the scan); a key that has to be read, a workspace’s map, is waited for up to 35 s, and the answer says how far it got if not; section cuts it open for the picture alone. 800 px on the long side by default, up to 2048; views: two to six standard views in one picture. In the Deviation workspace the answer says which map is painted (map) or why none (mapWhy; mapNote when the reference ghost dulls the colours); empty says why a picture has nothing in it. Waits for the session to settle. Needs the viewport. The picture comes back as an image; with `path` it is written to a file too, and with `inline: false` only there.

instructions: These tools drive ScanRuler, a measuring app for 3D scans, in the browser tab the user has open: the user watches every step in the viewport and can undo it there. Start with scanruler_status. If no ScanRuler page is connected, call scanruler_open: it opens ScanRuler in the user’s browser, paired with this server, and waits for it. If that leaves it unconnected, tell the user what howToConnect says, then call scanruler_wait. Before a task’s first step, read its guide with guide_read — how to measure a scan, model a part or turn a scan into CAD, written for the ScanRuler build connected: guide_read with no topic lists the guides and their sections. Read session_state before acting and after: the scan’s bounding box says where the part lies, the elements and dimensions what is measured. Lengths are millimetres, angles degrees; answers give numbers to six significant digits. A place on the scan is { point: [x, y, z] } (the nearest scan vertex is taken) or { vertex: n }. To fit a feature, aim at its middle, not at an edge. Every tool that changes the session is one step of the undo history; history_undo takes the last back. report_get gives the report as JSON (format "json") or as the text the panel copies (format "text"). A change, a batch or a long read still running at the server’s answer limit (scanruler_status: server.answerWithin) answers { queued: true, job } and runs on: scanruler_wait { for: "job", job } gives its answer — call it again while it says running. view_render shows you the 3D view as a picture; view_set turns it to a standard view or fits it. scanruler_batch runs several tools in one call, in order — many scan_nearest or element_fit calls, say — and stops at the first that is refused unless told to go on.
